answer: Divergent-Challenge Identity Bridge: each identity must periodically solve a challenge whose answer depends on its full interaction history, then post the result to a shared verification bridge. Clones replay identical histories, so their answers collide and only one survives deduplication. An attacker must maintain genuinely divergent behavior per identity, like separate branches on a trellis, paying real compute and storage to keep each fork distinct. Colluding clones that mirror each other are pruned, and the surviving pearl of each cluster absorbs the cost.
